subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: Should WebChat/Codex sends force-rotate stale native threads, fail fast visibly, or preserve the immediate ACK contract and rely on recovery when native Codex cannot prove a runnable turn?
rationale: The remaining choice changes the public `chat.send` liveness contract and Codex app-server thread ownership; source inspection shows adjacent mitigations but no proof of the desired product behavior for the reported wedge.

options.title: Require Runnable-Or-Visible Before ACK
options.body: Return `started` only after the Codex dispatch path has a runnable turn or has converted the failure into a visible persisted error; this best matches the user-safety requirement.

options.title: Force-Rotate Stale Native Threads
options.body: Treat over-budget or stale native bindings as unsafe and clear them before resume, accepting possible context loss to avoid silent stuck sessions.

options.title: Keep Recovery-Only Semantics
options.body: Leave immediate ACK behavior intact and add diagnostics/doctor recovery only, accepting that users may still see delayed or manual recovery for this class.

recommendation.title: Require Runnable-Or-Visible Before ACK
recommendation.body: Return `started` only after the Codex dispatch path has a runnable turn or has converted the failure into a visible persisted error; this best matches the user-safety requirement.

likelyOwner.reason: They have adjacent history on both non-blocking WebChat send semantics and Codex compaction recovery, making them the best available owner for the product boundary choice.
